title: A tool screenshot is evidence of a configuration, not of a result: read the inputs, the status and the empty result pane
summary: Two posters show a desktop tool at the start of a run: a nominal simulation against ignition-delay targets and an ignition-delay sensitivity calculation. The frames show the inputs and a running status. What the inputs mean, and what the finished run is for, is standard combustion-kinetics practice.

media.alt: Screenshot of a desktop application window titled Nominal Simulation. A banner reads Run one named nominal simulation. A left panel Run configuration holds fields: run label nominal_htc, mechanism, targets, target count 30, thermo file, transport file, base .opt template, an Advanced section, a Run button and a status box reading Running: nominal_htc. The right panel has a Tables tab that is empty.

read_the_figure.question: What was the tool asked to compute, with which inputs, and what has it done so far?
read_the_figure.axes: Not a plot. The window has a title banner, a left Run configuration form (labels on the left, values in the boxes), a Run button and a status box at the bottom left, and a right result area with tabs (Tables or Results). The status bar at the bottom reads mso-studio v0.1.0 and, in the second poster, Running.
look_at: Nominal Simulation: run label nominal_htc, target count 30, the mechanism, targets, thermo and transport files, and a base .opt template. The status says Running: nominal_htc, and the Tables tab is empty because nothing has finished.

Sensitivity analysis: two technique tabs (brute-force on a target file, and ignition-delay sensitivity). The active one has fuel H2, oxidiser O2:1.0, N2:3.76 (air), initial T 1200 K, pressure 13.5 atm, equivalence ratio 1.00, constant-volume reactor, method brute, top 20 reactions.
The status line names the case: h2o2_he_phi1.0_T1200_P13.5, so the case label records the three condition values.
The result tab is empty in both frames: they document the setup, not the outcome.
read_the_figure.proves: That the tool exposes standard kinetics calculations and that the run was configured with the inputs shown. It proves nothing about numerical results.
if_wrong: A path cut off at the left of a box hides which file was used: scroll or widen the field before trusting it.
A screenshot taken at the start of a run can be mistaken for a finished one: check the result pane and the status.
An unlabelled default (for example the reactor type) can change the answer: confirm each field.
must_check: Every input that changes the numbers is visible: mechanism, composition, T, P, phi, reactor type, method.
Units are given beside values (K, atm: yes).
The status says Running or Done, and the result pane matches.
The software version is visible (mso-studio v0.1.0: yes).
File paths are readable or described in the caption.
as_drawn: Sensitivity form: T 1200 K, P 13.5 atm, phi 1.0, reactor constV, method brute, top-N 20, fuel H2, oxidiser O2:1.0 N2:3.76.
For hydrogen in air at phi = 1 the hydrogen mole fraction is 2 / (2 + 1 + 3.76) = 0.296 (computed): the form gives only the ratios, the mole fractions follow from phi.

terms.meaning: A run of the mechanism with its published (unperturbed) rate parameters, compared against target data. It is the baseline against which any tuning is judged.
A list of species and elementary reactions with rate parameters and thermodynamic data, in a file read by the simulator.
A measured or reference ignition delay at a given temperature, pressure and mixture, used to judge a mechanism.
The fractional change of an output per fractional change of a rate constant, here the ignition delay tau and a rate constant k.
Perturb one rate constant, rerun the simulation and difference the results. Simple and robust but costs one extra run per reaction.
A closed adiabatic vessel of fixed volume, the usual model of a shock tube or rapid-compression machine for ignition delay.
Fuel-to-oxidiser ratio relative to the stoichiometric ratio; 1 means balanced.

remember: Brute-force sensitivity needs one extra simulation per reaction, plus the baseline.
Sensitivity of ignition delay is negative for reactions that speed ignition and positive for those that slow it.
For a screenshot, ask what is visible, what is cut off, and what has finished.
Air is O2 : N2 = 1 : 3.76 by moles.
The case label should carry the condition: here phi, T and P are in the name.

understand.title: What the tool does
understand.text: The nominal simulation calculates the model's predictions at the target conditions so they can be compared with the targets. The sensitivity tool answers a different question: which reactions control the result at one condition, which tells you where a rate constant would have to change to move the prediction.

understand.title: Why the sensitivity form needs so few inputs
understand.text: The ignition delay depends only on the mechanism, the initial mixture and temperature, the pressure and the reactor model. The form lists exactly those, plus the method and the number of reactions to report.

understand.title: Reading a recording honestly
understand.text: A poster frame cannot show the result. The recording matters because it shows the run finishing; the poster is evidence only of the setup and should be cited as such.

steps.title: Definition of the sensitivity
steps.note: A dimensionless number: S = -1 means doubling k roughly halves the delay (to first order).

steps.title: Brute-force estimate
steps.note: Run once with k multiplied by 1 + epsilon (for example 1.05) and difference the logs. One run per reaction plus one baseline, which is why the tool asks for a top-N list.

steps.title: Central version
steps.note: A symmetric difference has an error of second order in epsilon instead of first, at the cost of one more run per reaction.

steps.title: Cost of the study
steps.note: The hydrogen mechanism bundled with Cantera has a few tens of reactions, so the study is quick; a large hydrocarbon mechanism would need thousands of runs.

steps.title: Composition of H2 in air at phi = 1
steps.note: Stoichiometry 2 H2 + O2 fixes 2 mol of fuel per mole of oxygen; air adds 3.76 mol of nitrogen per mole of oxygen.

steps.title: Sign logic
steps.note: A faster chain-branching step makes radicals sooner and shortens the delay; a chain-terminating step removes radicals and lengthens it. The reasoning is standard; the actual coefficients are in the finished result, not in the poster.

worked.title: How many runs for a brute-force study?
worked.problem: A mechanism has 29 reactions. How many simulations does a forward-difference brute-force sensitivity need, and how many with a central difference?

solution.text: Forward: one baseline plus one perturbed run per reaction.
Central: one baseline plus two perturbed runs per reaction (or two per reaction without the baseline).

worked.answer: 30 runs forward, 59 central. The tool's top-N list only truncates the report, not the number of runs.

analyze.q: The sensitivity form asks for T, P, phi and reactor type but not for a time span. Why is that enough to define the answer?
analyze.hint: The delay is the output; the run ends at ignition.

analyze.q: What could you not conclude from the nominal-simulation poster even though it says Running?
analyze.hint: Nothing about results, accuracy or run time.

analyze.q: How do the case label and the form fields serve as a check on each other?
analyze.hint: phi1.0, T1200, P13.5 in the label against the values in the form.

evaluate.q: Is a screenshot at the start of a run good documentation for a tool? List what it documents well and what it cannot.
Which of the form's inputs would you want to see stated in a caption for a reader who cannot read the cut-off file paths?
evaluate.hint: The mechanism name, the target set, and the reactor assumptions.

create: Write the caption for the sensitivity poster so it states the condition, the method and what the finished ranking will mean, without quoting numbers.
Design a one-slide storyboard of the recording: setup, run, result table, interpretation.

checks.q: What does a sensitivity coefficient of -1 mean?
checks.hint: d ln tau / d ln k.
checks.answer: A one percent increase in the rate constant shortens the ignition delay by about one percent.

checks.q: A mechanism has 50 reactions. How many runs for a forward brute-force study?
checks.answer: 51 runs (one baseline plus one per reaction).

checks.q: Why is a chain-branching reaction expected to have a negative sensitivity?
checks.answer: A faster branching step grows the radical pool sooner, so ignition happens earlier and the delay falls.

checks.q: The poster shows an empty Tables tab and the status Running. What may be concluded?
checks.answer: Only that the run was started with the shown configuration. Nothing about its outcome.

checks.q: How would you present the finished sensitivity ranking?
checks.answer: A horizontal bar chart of the top reactions sorted by absolute coefficient, with sign colours, the condition in the title and the perturbation size in the caption.
